# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo xtask ci`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gate case.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Work on `kition-slide` only in its main checkout; never change, build, or commit in its worktrees (`kition-slide-wt/*`, `kition-*-wt`, `kition-naming-work`).
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.pdf` kit. These rules come first; the upstream rules below
still apply to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/kit-editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with Kition PDF's tool tabs, the page canvas, page thumbnails, bookmarks, comments, and form fields; a host (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows it
  in an iframe and talks to it over the Kit UI protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, kition-sdk `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only with the host's theme tokens and kit-editor components;
  ribbon labels and command titles are the upstream editor's English text, translated by its
  `web/src/i18n/upstream` catalogs and, where those lack a label, by `PHRASES` in
  `web/src/strings.ts` (with the editor's own `en-US` and `zh-CN` strings). Files go only
  through the host.
- `bindings/wasm` compiles the engine to WebAssembly on the public `KitionAI/kition-sdk`
  crate; the editor runs it in a Web Worker. The contract and the Kition platform rules live in kition-sdk
  (`docs/platform/kits/engine.md`, `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`), the agent protocol
  in KHP ([`kitharness/kitharness`](https://github.com/kitharness/kitharness));
  change them there, never here. `kition-pdf-kit` must keep passing `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`,
  and `kit.json` must pass kition-sdk's `tools/check-manifest.mjs`.
- The kit has no pointer tools yet: Kition shows the pages and the kit's commands, which are Kition PDF's automation tools. Never draw editor chrome into the rendered pixels.
- The whole repository is Apache-2.0 ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); third-party notices are listed in `NOTICE`.
  Upstream is credited only in `NOTICE`; never write upstream names anywhere else.

# AGENTS.md — rules for every agent and contributor

These rules bind every AI agent and every human contributor working in this repository. They come before any task, instruction or deadline. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` holds the day-to-day working instructions. If the two ever disagree, **this file wins.**

See `docs/kits.md` in the Kition repository and kition-sdk's `docs/platform/` for the shared conventions this repository follows.

---

## 1. Asset policy (absolute — no exceptions)

An **asset** is any non-code material that the project includes, ships, embeds, generates for publication, or shows in its documentation. This covers:
- icons, images, illustrations, screenshots and logos;
- fonts;
- colour profiles and other binary data files;
- sounds and video;
- sample, demo and test documents that are committed or published;
- anything the app renders from those.

### 1.1 Nothing from Adobe products

- **Never** use icons, images, artwork, logos, UI graphics, fonts, stamps, cursors, sample documents or any other asset taken from an Adobe product, installer, website, document or package.
  - "Adobe product" includes Acrobat, Reader, Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom and Creative Cloud, including the fonts they install (for example Minion, Myriad, Kozuka and the Adobe CJK families).
  - This holds even when Adobe publishes the material under an open licence, if it is **visual design**. For example, **do not** use Source Han, Source Serif or Source Sans, or Noto CJK, which is Source Han rebranded.
  - **One exception, by the user's decision (2026-11-17): Shippori Mincho** (OFL-1.1, no Reserved Font Name), the serif face for Japanese document text. Its kana are FONTDASU's own, but its kanji come from Genryu Mincho, a derivative of Source Han Serif. It comes only from kition-fonts (§1.4), whose `ATTRIBUTION.md` states that lineage; the build's barred families (`crates/support/fonts/build.rs`) still bar Source Han itself. No other Source Han derivative is allowed, and adding one needs the user's explicit approval.
- **Never** recreate, trace, redraw or closely imitate an Adobe icon or graphic. Our icons come from Lucide, and our visual design is our own.
- Screenshots of Adobe software exist only as private, local observation notes under `plan/acrobat/`, which is gitignored. They must **never** be committed, published, linked, shown in docs, used as a design source to trace, or placed anywhere else in the repository or its outputs.
- The only Adobe-authored material allowed is **non-visual technical data** that is openly licensed and required for PDF compatibility. Each item needs its own entry in `docs/attribution.toml` with `adobe_data = true`, and the list below is closed:
  - The CMap resources (BSD-3-Clause), bundled inside the `hayro-cmap` dependency.
  - The standard-14 font metrics and encoding tables in the PDF specification. They are data, not typefaces, and are embedded as code in hayro.

  Adding anything to this list needs the user's explicit approval.

### 1.2 Only open, provable licences

Every asset must be one of:
- **Open source:** ISC, MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, OFL-1.1, Ubuntu-Font-1.0 or Bitstream-Vera.
- **Creative Commons:** CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0 or CC-BY-SA-4.0.
- **Public domain.**
- **Contributor-original:** created, photographed or generated by a contributor who owns it and licenses it under the project licence (`Apache-2.0`).

Anything else is forbidden, including assets whose licence you cannot prove from the source. Examples:
- system fonts (Apple, Microsoft, Google Android system UI fonts that are not openly licensed);
- emoji artwork from Apple, Microsoft or Samsung;
- stock photos;
- "free for personal use" material;
- screenshots of other people's software.

**Screenshots of Kition PDF** are contributor-original. Everything visible in them must itself be allowed: our UI, Lucide icons, OFL fonts, and demo documents built only from allowed assets. Never screenshot a document that uses proprietary fonts or images.

### 1.3 Every asset is attributed

- **`docs/attribution.toml`** is the single source of truth. It has **one entry per asset file**, whether committed, vendored, fetched at build time or bundled through a Cargo dependency. Each entry records:
  - path or URL, title, author;
  - source (URL, with version or commit);
  - SPDX licence, and the licence file in the repo;
  - SHA-256;
  - how it is used.
- **`docs/attribution.md`** is generated from it (`cargo xtask assets --write`). Never edit it by hand.
- **`NOTICE`** keeps the licence notices that the licences require.
- **`cargo xtask assets`** runs in `cargo xtask ci`. It fails if:
  - an asset file in the repository has no entry;
  - an entry's hash does not match;
  - a licence is not on the allowlist;
  - a licence file is missing;
  - an image, icon or font names Adobe as author or source.
- **`cargo xtask demo-pdf`** downloads its fonts only from `docs/attribution.toml` entries, pinned by SHA-256. Afterwards it **fails if the PDF embeds any font not in its allowlist**, which catches the browser silently falling back to a system font.

### 1.4 Fonts live in kition-fonts

- Font assets, including every Japanese font, live in [`KitionAI/kition-fonts`](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-fonts), not here. **Never commit a font file to this repository**; adding a font means adding it to kition-fonts. (The Latin UI fonts in `assets/fonts/` — Inter, JetBrains Mono, Dancing Script — are the exception.)
- kition-fonts is an **optional build input**, never a Cargo dependency: `KITION_FONTS_DIR=<checkout> cargo build` makes `crates/support/fonts/build.rs` embed its fonts as `kition_pdf_fonts::KITION_FONTS`. Without it Kition PDF builds, tests and runs, but has no Japanese face (Japanese UI text shows replacement boxes, and writing Japanese into a PDF returns a clear error). Release builds set it, and `docs/attribution.toml` lists it as a `[[build_input]]`.

### 1.5 Procedure for adding or changing an asset

Fonts go to kition-fonts instead (§1.4).

1. Find an asset under an allowed licence from its **original source**: the author's repository or a release, not a random mirror. Record the exact version or commit.
2. Confirm the authorship. It must not be Adobe (§1.1). Keep the licence text.
3. Add the file together with its licence file, plus a `docs/attribution.toml` entry. Run `cargo xtask assets --write`, then `cargo xtask assets`.
4. If an asset's origin or licence is unclear, **do not add it.** Ask the user.

If you find an asset that breaks these rules, stop and remove it from the repository and every output, including docs, screenshots and generated PDFs. Then tell the user at once.

## 2. Clean-room rules (summary; details in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `plan/adr/0001`)

- Never read, disassemble or copy anything inside the Acrobat bundle. Only names and listings are allowed, and **never** open `Contents/Resources/JavaScripts/`.
- Behaviour comes only from public specifications (ISO 32000-2, the Arlington model), public documentation and black-box observation.
- Never copy GPL/AGPL code. Copyleft tools run only as external oracle processes.
- Observe Acrobat only with synthetic fixtures. Never capture personal data, account information or recent files.
- Never commit large binary test-oracle fixtures to this repository; fetch them pinned by commit and sha256-verified instead.

## 3. Agent control (automation)

- **Everything is reachable headlessly.** Every user-facing feature must be callable without a
  GUI: an engine API, then a tool in `crates/engine/automation`, which `kition-pdf-kit` (the in-page
  WebAssembly engine) and `bindings/headless` (the headless executable Kition's agent drives over
  the `kition-kit/1` protocol) both reach through the same table. A feature is not done until
  its tool exists and has an end-to-end test (`crates/engine/automation/README.md`, "Adding a tool").
- **Safe by default.** Tools must never discard unsaved work silently, must write atomically, must honour `--root`, and must return errors an agent can act on (say what was wrong and what is allowed).
- **Track parity honestly.** Every user-facing feature has an entry in `tools/parity/acrobat-features.toml`. Mark it `shipped` only when it works end to end and the entry cites a passing test (`evidence`); `cargo xtask parity` (part of `xtask ci`) rejects claims whose commands, tools or tests don't exist.
- **Use it to test.** Agents should drive the engine through the automation tools and look at `page_render` output to check their own changes. For UI changes, look at the real editor (`cd web && pnpm dev`, or `pnpm test:flow`).

## 4. Never crash

Kition PDF opens files from strangers, and people trust it with their work. A malformed PDF, a bad tool argument, a corrupt settings file or a full disk must produce an error the user (or agent) can act on, never a crash and never lost work. **This outranks feature work:** don't ship a feature by adding a panic path, and fix a crash before building on top of it.

- **Fail with `Result`.** Non-test code returns errors through the crate's error type and `?`. Where readers are lenient by design, fall back gracefully and record the repair (see Fidelity in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`).
- **No panicking shortcuts.** No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or `unimplemented!` outside tests, unless the call is provably infallible (e.g. writing to a `Vec`), with a comment saying why. `assert!` only for internal invariants that input cannot reach.
- **No `unsafe`.** The workspace sets `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. If a platform API needs it, use a maintained safe wrapper crate; a real exception needs a maintainer's sign-off.
- **Treat every input-derived number as hostile.** Use `get()` instead of `[i]` or `[a..b]`. Slice strings only at char boundaries. Use checked/saturating arithmetic for lengths, offsets and counts. Guard against division by zero and NaN/inf casts, and never cast a negative value to `usize`. Cap allocations sized by the file.
- **Bound recursion.** Object graphs can be cyclic or deeply nested. Walk them with seen-sets or depth limits.
- **Don't cascade.** Handle lock poisoning, and keep a panic in a worker thread from taking the app down. Engine entry points that run untrusted-document code keep their last-resort `catch_unwind` guard, and command execution and file import/export must sit behind one that turns an escaped panic into an error message and keeps the user's document. Keep `panic = "unwind"` (the default) so the guard works. It is a safety net, not a substitute for the rules above.
- **Prove it.** Every crash fix comes with a small synthetic regression test that panicked before the fix.
- **Enforced by clippy.** Root `.clippy.toml` lets tests use `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`. A crate that is clean carries `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`; new crates start with it.

## 5. Everything else


Follow `.claude/CLAUDE.md`. It covers quality gates, layering, commit rules and how to run and look at the app.
